sections.heading: NewDermaMed Team
sections.text: NewDermaMed Team Scroll down to view our full team of highly trained and experienced cosmetic surgeons and medical professionals. Dr. Negin Mastouri Medical Director/ Aesthetic Doctor See More Dr. Luis Figueroa Vascular Surgeon See More Alin Gharibian Clinic Director/Cosmetic Consultant See More Dr. Negin Mastouri Medical Director/ Aesthetic Doctor Dr. Negin Mastouri is an accomplished Medical Director and Aesthetic Doctor with a passion for helping her clients achieve their best selves. She is a graduate of the prestigious University of Toronto and is board-certified in Family Medicine with a clinical fellowship in Hospital Medicine. Dr. Mastouri is also an international board-certified specialist in Infectious Disease, with a particular focus on infection prevention and control. With a special interest in skin disorders, aesthetic medicine, and women’s health, Dr. Mastouri is dedicated to providing personalized, preventive, and predictive healthcare to her clients. She is a Fellow in Metabolic and Nutritional Medicine (FMNM) and a proud member of the American Academy of Anti-Aging Medicine. What sets Dr. Mastouri apart is her holistic, wellness-oriented approach to patient care. She uses the latest scientific breakthroughs and takes an interdisciplinary approach to help her clients achieve optimal health and well-being. Dr. Mastouri is also an Assistant Professor at McMaster University, where she shares her knowledge and expertise with the next generation of medical professionals. Whether you’re looking for a specific treatment or want to take a more comprehensive approach to your health, Dr. Mastouri is here to help. Dr. Mastouri’s expertise in advanced facial rejuvenation and Botox techniques enables her to offer personalized cosmetic treatments that enhance natural beauty and create a refreshed appearance. Using advanced dermal fillers, injectables, and laser therapies, she addresses a range of cosmetic concerns while also providing specialized treatments for skin issues like acne and hyperpigmentation. With a focus on safety and effectiveness, Dr. Mastouri works closely with each client to develop a personalized treatment plan that aligns with their goals and needs. Her passion for aesthetic medicine drives her to stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in cosmetic treatments and techniques. Dr. Luis Figueroa Vascular Surgeon Dr. Figueroa is a practicing vascular surgeon and a fellow at The Royal College of Surgeons of Canada. He graduated from The University of Toronto, Vascular Surgery Program, and thereafter joined the division as a lecturer. Dr. Figueroa has practiced vascular surgery at Toronto’s Humber River Hospital and North Toronto Vascular Surgery. Alin Gharibian Clinic Director/Cosmetic Consultant Certified in Cosmetic Dermatology & Medical AestheticsWith a Bachelor of Science in Biology and advanced certifications in Cosmetic Dermatology and Medical Aesthetics, Alin Gharibian is a skilled expert in anti-aging and skin rejuvenation treatments. Specialized training in anti-aging therapies ensures the delivery of innovative, evidence-based solutions tailored to meet each client’s unique needs. As the Director of NewDermaMed, Alin leads with a dedication to excellence, blending scientific knowledge with a personalized touch. This commitment has established NewDermaMed as a trusted destination for achieving natural, youthful results through advanced cosmetic treatments. Driven by a passion for enhancing confidence and well-being, Alin remains at the forefront of the medical aesthetics industry. By combining cutting-edge science with artistry and compassion, every treatment is designed to empower and inspire confidence in clients. Abbas Ashrafsadeh IMG, Aesthetic Physician (UAE) Abbas Ashrafzadeh, a Dubai-based aesthetic physician with 20+ years of experience, has treated over 1000+ Aptos Thread Lift procedures including celebrities seeking subtle, flawless cosmetic enhancements.

sections.heading: Your Top Questions, Answered
sections.text: Your Top Questions, Answered Everything you need to know before starting your journey with us. Claim your FREE Consultation today — meet directly with our certified specialists BOOK MY FREE CONSULTATION CALL US NOW Your Top Questions, Answered What treatments are available at NewDermaMed Clinic? NewDermaMed specializes in advanced non-surgical medical aesthetics. Services include laser hair removal, Botox® and dermal fillers, acne and scar treatments, skin tightening, medical facials, body contouring, chemical peels, and skin rejuvenation with microneedling and PRP. What devices and technologies does the clinic use? The clinic uses state-of-the-art, Health Canada–approved medical devices. These include Candela GentleMax Pro for laser hair removal, Cutera Excel V+ for vascular and pigmentation treatments, Morpheus8 for skin tightening and collagen stimulation, and CoolSculpting® for non-surgical fat reduction. Are the treatments safe and effective? Yes. All treatments are performed by trained medical professionals using FDA and Health Canada–approved devices and products. Treatment plans are customized to your skin type and goals to ensure safe, predictable, and natural-looking results. How do I book a consultation? You can book a free consultation by calling the clinic directly, filling out the online booking form on NewDermaMed’s website, or visiting the clinic in person. During your consultation, a specialist will assess your needs and recommend the most suitable treatment options.

Claim your FREE Consultation today — meet directly with our certified specialists BOOK MY FREE CONSULTATION CALL US NOW Your Top Questions, Answered How do I check the price of a treatment? You can view pricing by expanding the treatment categories listed on the pricing page (e.g., Botox, Dermal Fillers, Coolsculpting, Microneedling, etc.). Each category shows detailed costs and current offers. Are the prices the same at all locations? Yes, the listed prices and promotions apply across all participating clinic locations unless otherwise noted. Do promotions apply to pricing? Yes. Current promotions (such as up to 60% off Hyperpigmentation, 60% off Laser Hair Removal, and 40% off Dermal Fillers) are reflected in the pricing section. Are consultations included in the pricing? Yes, consultations are free. This ensures your provider can assess your needs and customize the treatment plan before confirming final pricing. Is financing available for treatments? Yes. posts.title: What Causes Rosacea Redness
posts.excerpt: You’re not the only one who has noticed that your face is always red, flushed, or has tiny visible blood vessels and wondered what could be causing it. Rosacea is a condition that often causes redness and swelling in the middle of the face. To treat it effectively, you need to know what causes this […]
posts.content_html_rest:
You’re not the only one who has noticed that your face is always red, flushed, or has tiny visible blood vessels and wondered what could be causing it. Rosacea is a condition that often causes redness and swelling in the middle of the face. To treat it effectively, you need to know what causes this redness. Many of our patients at NewDermamed are upset about how unpredictable and visible rosacea redness can be, from the cheeks and nose to the chin and forehead. In this article, we’ll talk about what rosacea redness really is, what biological and environmental factors make it worse, how to spot the things that make it worse, and how we treat and manage it in a way that works for each person.

Getting to Know Rosacea Redness

What does rosacea redness look like

Rosacea is a long-term inflammatory skin condition that mostly affects the middle of the face. Persistent redness (erythema) is at the heart of the problem. It is often followed by flushing, visible small blood vessels (telangiectasia), and sometimes bumps or pustules. The flushing can turn into a more constant redness over time, and the skin may feel warm, sore, or sensitive.

What causes the redness

Researchers don’t know what causes rosacea, but they think it has something to do with changes in the immune system, problems with the skin barrier, and things in the environment. To put it another way, the blood vessels in the face may open up and stay open more easily, the skin’s protective barrier becomes more sensitive, and inflammatory processes start more easily. These changes make the redness that we see and feel.

Who gets it and how often does it happen

Rosacea can affect anyone, but it is most common in adults between the ages of 30 and 60. It is also more likely to happen to people with fair skin, though it can happen to people with any skin tone. It seems that men and women are affected in about the same numbers, but the way it looks and how embarrassed or upset they feel may be different. The best way to manage redness is to catch it early, before more serious signs show up.

Main Reasons for Rosacea Redness

Genetic and hereditary elements

There is a lot of proof that rosacea runs in families. If someone in your family has this condition, you are more likely to get it. Your genes may affect how your blood vessels work, how your skin barrier responds to stress, and how your immune system works.

Triggers for vascular and neurovascular

Hyperreactivity of blood vessels and nerve reflexes is one of the main causes of rosacea redness. In a lot of people with rosacea, the blood vessels in their facial skin open up too easily when they are exposed to heat, alcohol, spicy food, or the sun. This causes redness and flushing. Also, some receptors in the skin may be too active, which means that your skin will react more strongly to things that normal skin would ignore.

Immune and inflammatory processes

Aberrant immune responses also contribute. Some individuals with rosacea exhibit elevated immune proteins, heightened inflammatory markers, and, in certain instances, an overpopulation of skin mites such as Demodex, which may provoke inflammation. These immune factors can make the redness last longer and make the skin more sensitive.

Problems with the skin barrier

The condition of the skin’s barrier is also very important. When the skin barrier is damaged by the sun, harsh skin care, stress from the environment, or age, the face is more likely to get irritated, and flushing can become a permanent feature instead of a brief blush.

Skin connections between microbes and the gut

New research shows that some microbes, like skin mites and even an imbalance of gut bacteria, may be linked to rosacea. Even though bacteria don’t directly cause redness, they can make inflammation and blood vessel responsiveness worse, which can make the redness worse or more frequent.

Things in the environment and your lifestyle that can cause problems

External triggers are a big reason why rosacea makes the skin red. These don’t cause rosacea directly, but they can make the skin flare up and get redder in someone who is already prone to it. Some things that can set off an outbreak are being in the sun, being in very hot or cold weather, being in the wind, drinking alcohol, eating spicy foods, drinking hot drinks, being stressed out, working out hard, and some skin care products. Knowing what makes you red is an important part of managing it well.

Understanding How Redness Shows Up

Flushing and redness that comes and goes in the early stages

At first, redness might come and go in bursts or episodes. You might blush more easily, and your face might get warm and red after something happens, but then it goes away. This is often the first sign of rosacea.

Constant redness and visible blood vessels

As the condition gets worse, the flushing episodes may turn into a more permanent redness. You might be able to see small blood vessels just under the skin. At this point, the redness is harder to get rid of, so you need a plan to deal with it.

Changes and problems that are more serious

In cases that have been going on for a long time, the redness may be accompanied by bumps, pustules, thickened skin, especially on the nose, and even eye involvement. A bulbous nose from thickening tissue and long-term redness is one of the most obvious signs of advanced disease. So, it’s important to act quickly while the redness is still manageable.

Recognizing Your Triggers and Redness Patterns

Common trigger types

To lessen the redness of rosacea, you need to know what makes it worse. Some of the most common things that set them off are:

  • Sunlight or UV rays
  • Spicy foods and hot drinks
  • Drinks with alcohol, like red wine
  • Very hot and very cold weather
  • Stress from emotions
  • Working out and doing hard physical work
  • Products for skin care or makeup that make the skin red
  • Wind, heat, humidity, or heating or cooling systems inside

Writing down your triggers

We tell our patients at NewDermamed to keep a simple diary of their flare-ups. Write down what you ate or drank, the weather, the skincare you used, how you felt emotionally, any alcohol you drank, and how your skin reacted. You can see patterns over time. You can avoid or lessen your high-risk triggers once you know what they are. This will make redness less common and less severe.

Knowing how people are different

Keep in mind that what makes one person red may not make another person red. Some people are more sensitive to food, while others are more sensitive to temperature or skin care. Personalized tracking and management are the most important things.

How Newdermamed Treats Rosacea Redness

Step 1: A full evaluation of the skin and its history

At NewDermamed, we start by learning about your skin type, your history of redness or flushing, your family history, and how you live your life. We figure out how much of the redness is caused by changes in blood vessels and how much is caused by inflammation or problems with the skin barrier. This helps us make a plan that fits your specific reasons for being red.

Step 2: Managing your lifestyle and triggers

From day one we focus on nonmedical strategies such as strict daily sun protection with SPF, gentle skincare that avoids fragrance and irritants, identifying and avoiding known personal triggers, and supporting the skin barrier with soothing ingredients. These basic steps help lower the redness baseline and make any medical or procedural treatments work better.

Step 3: Medical and topical treatments

If the redness is mild, we may suggest topical medications like azelaic acid, metronidazole, or brimonidine, which narrow blood vessels. If the redness is more severe, we may suggest ivermectin. Low-dose doxycycline and other oral medications can also help because they reduce inflammation. If you have blood vessels that are more visible or redness that won’t go away, vascular-targeted therapy like laser or intense pulsed light (IPL) can help a lot.

Step 4: Advanced therapies and procedures

Vascular laser therapy or IPL can help calm down redness that won’t go away by targeting superficial blood vessels and making them less visible. We always talk about realistic outcomes and ongoing care because rosacea tends to last a long time and needs to be cared for all the time.

Step 5: Maintenance and follow-up

We stress long-term care at NewDermamed because rosacea is a long-term condition. If you’ve had laser or IPL therapy, we keep an eye on your redness, change your plan for avoiding triggers, go over your medications, and set up maintenance sessions. We want to keep the redness down and the skin healthy and calm.

Helpful Tips to Calm Down Rosacea Redness

Gentle skin care and help with barriers

Avoid scrubs and harsh exfoliants, and use gentle, non-foaming cleansers. Look for moisturizers that have ceramides, niacinamide, and panthenol in them to help protect your skin. Stay away from things that have alcohol, menthol, or a strong smell.

Keep the sun and the outside world from hurting your skin

Every day, put on sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher. When you’re outside, wear a hat or find some shade. Use a scarf or protective cream to protect your skin when it’s cold or windy.

Be careful about what you eat and how you live

Write down the foods and drinks that make you red in a trigger diary. Common culprits include spicy food, hot beverages, alcohol, and caffeine. Relaxation or mindfulness can help you deal with stress, since emotional flushing is a real trigger. If hot baths or saunas make your skin flare up, stay away from them.

Pick your skincare and makeup carefully

Use makeup that is made with minerals and is safe for sensitive skin. Choose brands that dermatologists recommend and don’t use too many active ingredients at once. Add new products slowly and test them on a small area first when you can.

Get professional help as soon as possible

If the redness doesn’t go away or makes you feel less confident, get help from a professional. At NewDermamed, early diagnosis and treatment are very important for avoiding long-term problems.

Why It’s Not Just About Looks

Rosacea’s constant redness is more than just a cosmetic issue. It shows changes in the biology of your skin, like how blood vessels work, how your immune system works, how your skin barrier breaks down, and how sensitive it gets. If you don’t treat it, the redness can get worse and show up as visible vessels, thicker skin, and even eye problems. Your skin’s health and appearance will stay good if you treat it early and consistently.

Conclusion

To get calmer, clearer skin, you need to first understand what causes rosacea redness. At NewDermamed, we think that dealing with redness needs a careful, individualized plan that includes changes to your lifestyle, gentle skin care, and, when necessary, medical and laser therapy. Our staff is committed to helping you feel good about your skin again with treatments that are right for your skin type and way of life. Call NewDermamed today to set up your consultation and start your journey toward healthier, more radiant skin if you’re ready to take charge of your redness.

To put it another way, the blood vessels in the face may open up and stay open more easily, the skin’s protective barrier becomes more sensitive, and inflammatory processes start more easily. These changes make the redness that we see and feel.

Who gets it and how often does it happen

Rosacea can affect anyone, but it is most common in adults between the ages of 30 and 60. It is also more likely to happen to people with fair skin, though it can happen to people with any skin tone. It seems that men and women are affected in about the same numbers, but the way it looks and how embarrassed or upset they feel may be different. The best way to manage redness is to catch it early, before more serious signs show up.

Main Reasons for Rosacea Redness

Genetic and hereditary elements

There is a lot of proof that rosacea runs in families. If someone in your family has this condition, you are more likely to get it. Your genes may affect how your blood vessels work, how your skin barrier responds to stress, and how your immune system works.

Triggers for vascular and neurovascular

Hyperreactivity of blood vessels and nerve reflexes is one of the main causes of rosacea redness. In a lot of people with rosacea, the blood vessels in their facial skin open up too easily when they are exposed to heat, alcohol, spicy food, or the sun. This causes redness and flushing. Also, some receptors in the skin may be too active, which means that your skin will react more strongly to things that normal skin would ignore.

Immune and inflammatory processes

Aberrant immune responses also contribute. Some individuals with rosacea exhibit elevated immune proteins, heightened inflammatory markers, and, in certain instances, an overpopulation of skin mites such as Demodex, which may provoke inflammation. These immune factors can make the redness last longer and make the skin more sensitive.

Problems with the skin barrier

The condition of the skin’s barrier is also very important. When the skin barrier is damaged by the sun, harsh skin care, stress from the environment, or age, the face is more likely to get irritated, and flushing can become a permanent feature instead of a brief blush.

Skin connections between microbes and the gut

New research shows that some microbes, like skin mites and even an imbalance of gut bacteria, may be linked to rosacea. Even though bacteria don’t directly cause redness, they can make inflammation and blood vessel responsiveness worse, which can make the redness worse or more frequent.

Things in the environment and your lifestyle that can cause problems

External triggers are a big reason why rosacea makes the skin red. These don’t cause rosacea directly, but they can make the skin flare up and get redder in someone who is already prone to it. Some things that can set off an outbreak are being in the sun, being in very hot or cold weather, being in the wind, drinking alcohol, eating spicy foods, drinking hot drinks, being stressed out, working out hard, and some skin care products. Knowing what makes you red is an important part of managing it well.

Understanding How Redness Shows Up

Flushing and redness that comes and goes in the early stages

At first, redness might come and go in bursts or episodes. You might blush more easily, and your face might get warm and red after something happens, but then it goes away. This is often the first sign of rosacea.

Constant redness and visible blood vessels

As the condition gets worse, the flushing episodes may turn into a more permanent redness. You might be able to see small blood vessels just under the skin. At this point, the redness is harder to get rid of, so you need a plan to deal with it.

Changes and problems that are more serious

In cases that have been going on for a long time, the redness may be accompanied by bumps, pustules, thickened skin, especially on the nose, and even eye involvement. A bulbous nose from thickening tissue and long-term redness is one of the most obvious signs of advanced disease. So, it’s important to act quickly while the redness is still manageable.

Recognizing Your Triggers and Redness Patterns

Common trigger types

To lessen the redness of rosacea, you need to know what makes it worse. Some of the most common things that set them off are:

  • Sunlight or UV rays
  • Spicy foods and hot drinks
  • Drinks with alcohol, like red wine
  • Very hot and very cold weather
  • Stress from emotions
  • Working out and doing hard physical work
  • Products for skin care or makeup that make the skin red
  • Wind, heat, humidity, or heating or cooling systems inside

Writing down your triggers

We tell our patients at NewDermamed to keep a simple diary of their flare-ups. Write down what you ate or drank, the weather, the skincare you used, how you felt emotionally, any alcohol you drank, and how your skin reacted. You can see patterns over time. You can avoid or lessen your high-risk triggers once you know what they are. This will make redness less common and less severe.

Knowing how people are different

Keep in mind that what makes one person red may not make another person red. Some people are more sensitive to food, while others are more sensitive to temperature or skin care. Personalized tracking and management are the most important things.

How Newdermamed Treats Rosacea Redness

Step 1: A full evaluation of the skin and its history

At NewDermamed, we start by learning about your skin type, your history of redness or flushing, your family history, and how you live your life. We figure out how much of the redness is caused by changes in blood vessels and how much is caused by inflammation or problems with the skin barrier. This helps us make a plan that fits your specific reasons for being red.

Step 2: Managing your lifestyle and triggers

From day one we focus on nonmedical strategies such as strict daily sun protection with SPF, gentle skincare that avoids fragrance and irritants, identifying and avoiding known personal triggers, and supporting the skin barrier with soothing ingredients. These basic steps help lower the redness baseline and make any medical or procedural treatments work better.

Step 3: Medical and topical treatments

If the redness is mild, we may suggest topical medications like azelaic acid, metronidazole, or brimonidine, which narrow blood vessels. If the redness is more severe, we may suggest ivermectin. Low-dose doxycycline and other oral medications can also help because they reduce inflammation. If you have blood vessels that are more visible or redness that won’t go away, vascular-targeted therapy like laser or intense pulsed light (IPL) can help a lot.

Step 4: Advanced therapies and procedures

Vascular laser therapy or IPL can help calm down redness that won’t go away by targeting superficial blood vessels and making them less visible. We always talk about realistic outcomes and ongoing care because rosacea tends to last a long time and needs to be cared for all the time.

Step 5: Maintenance and follow-up

We stress long-term care at NewDermamed because rosacea is a long-term condition. If you’ve had laser or IPL therapy, we keep an eye on your redness, change your plan for avoiding triggers, go over your medications, and set up maintenance sessions. We want to keep the redness down and the skin healthy and calm.

Helpful Tips to Calm Down Rosacea Redness

Gentle skin care and help with barriers

Avoid scrubs and harsh exfoliants, and use gentle, non-foaming cleansers. Look for moisturizers that have ceramides, niacinamide, and panthenol in them to help protect your skin. Stay away from things that have alcohol, menthol, or a strong smell.

Keep the sun and the outside world from hurting your skin

Every day, put on sunscreen with an SPF of 30 or higher. When you’re outside, wear a hat or find some shade. Use a scarf or protective cream to protect your skin when it’s cold or windy.

Be careful about what you eat and how you live

Write down the foods and drinks that make you red in a trigger diary. Common culprits include spicy food, hot beverages, alcohol, and caffeine. Relaxation or mindfulness can help you deal with stress, since emotional flushing is a real trigger. If hot baths or saunas make your skin flare up, stay away from them.

Pick your skincare and makeup carefully

Use makeup that is made with minerals and is safe for sensitive skin. Choose brands that dermatologists recommend and don’t use too many active ingredients at once. Add new products slowly and test them on a small area first when you can.

Get professional help as soon as possible

If the redness doesn’t go away or makes you feel less confident, get help from a professional. At NewDermamed, early diagnosis and treatment are very important for avoiding long-term problems.

Why It’s Not Just About Looks

Rosacea’s constant redness is more than just a cosmetic issue. It shows changes in the biology of your skin, like how blood vessels work, how your immune system works, how your skin barrier breaks down, and how sensitive it gets. If you don’t treat it, the redness can get worse and show up as visible vessels, thicker skin, and even eye problems. Your skin’s health and appearance will stay good if you treat it early and consistently.

Conclusion

To get calmer, clearer skin, you need to first understand what causes rosacea redness. At NewDermamed, we think that dealing with redness needs a careful, individualized plan that includes changes to your lifestyle, gentle skin care, and, when necessary, medical and laser therapy. Our staff is committed to helping you feel good about your skin again with treatments that are right for your skin type and way of life. Call NewDermamed today to set up your consultation and start your journey toward healthier, more radiant skin if you’re ready to take charge of your redness.

posts.content_html_rest:
You’re in the right place if you’ve been thinking about never having hair again. In this blog post, we’ll go into great detail about laser hair removal, including how it works, how much it costs (especially in Toronto), how to choose the right clinic, and how to get ready for the best results. We at NewDermaMed believe that giving you information will help you make the best choice for your skin and way of life.

What Does It Mean to Have Laser Hair Removal?

Laser hair removal is a cosmetic procedure that uses a laser, which is a concentrated beam of light, to damage hair follicles. This slows down or stops hair growth over time.

Laser hair removal is better than shaving, waxing, or plucking because it permanently removes hair and makes skin smoother.

Why Should You Think About Laser Hair Removal?

Easy and Saves Time

Shaving, waxing, or tweezing all the time can get old. With laser hair removal, you won’t have to worry about unwanted hair as much and will be able to enjoy smooth results longer.

Results That Last Longer

No clinic can promise that every spot will be 100% hair-free, but many see permanent hair reduction over time.

Works in Many Places

Laser hair removal can get rid of hair on your legs, bikini line, underarms, back, face, and even your whole body.

How Does It Work?

The Science Behind Lasers

Laser systems send out light at specific wavelengths that the pigment (melanin) in the follicle absorbs. The heat damages the follicle and slows future growth.

Different lasers may be used for different tones and hair types. For example, Nd:YAG lasers work best on darker skin types.

Treatment Cycle and Why You Need More Than One Session

Hair grows in three phases: anagen, catagen, and telogen. Lasers only work on hairs in the anagen phase, meaning multiple sessions are needed to target all follicles over time.

What Happens in a Session?

  • Consultation/assessment
  • Pre-treatment instructions: no tanning or waxing; shave 1–2 days before
  • Protective eyewear and cooling systems during treatment
  • Redness or swelling for 1–3 days; avoid sun and use broad-spectrum SPF

What You Need to Know About Laser Hair Removal in Toronto

If you are searching for “laser hair removal near me” ,“laser hair removal Toronto downtown” or “full body laser hair removal Toronto price,” here are key things to consider.

Choosing a Clinic and Technology

Pick a clinic that has:

  • Medical supervision and trained professionals
  • Modern laser technology suitable for your skin and hair
  • Clear explanations of sessions, side effects, and aftercare

Things That Affect the Cost in Toronto

The price depends on:

  • Size of area treated
  • Hair color and thickness
  • Skin type
  • Number of sessions
  • Touch-up or maintenance fees

Average prices range from $60 to $400 per session depending on the area. Full-body packages often provide better value.

Questions to Ask During the Meeting

  • What kind of laser do you use?
  • How many sessions do I need?
  • Are touch-ups included?
  • What care is required before and after?
  • Are there hidden costs?
  • Can I see before-and-after photos?

Breakdown of Costs and What to Expect

Estimated Costs for Common Areas

  • Small areas (chin, upper lip): $60–$150
  • Medium areas (bikini, underarms): $150–$300
  • Large areas (legs, back, chest): $300–$400
  • Full body packages: more upfront but best long-term value

Number of Sessions and Total Cost

Most people need 3 to 8 sessions for the best results, depending on the area and hair density.

Saving Money Over Time

Laser hair removal costs more upfront but saves money long term by reducing the need for shaving and waxing.

The Pros and Cons of Laser Hair Removal

Pros

  • Long-lasting hair reduction
  • Softer, finer regrowth
  • Fewer ingrown hairs
  • Saves time
  • Smooth skin year-round

Possible Risks and Side Effects

  • Temporary redness or swelling
  • Mild irritation
  • Temporary pigmentation changes
  • Rare blistering if done incorrectly

How to Lower Risks

  • Choose a reputable clinic with medical supervision
  • Follow all pre- and post-care instructions
  • Avoid sun exposure
  • Inform your clinician of any medications or skin conditions

How to Pick the Right Clinic – What Makes NewDermaMed Different

Clear Prices and Honest Consultations

We provide transparent cost breakdowns and session expectations.

Customized Treatments for All Hair and Skin Types

Plans are tailored to your tone, texture, and treatment area.

The Best Safety Standards and Most Advanced Equipment

We use the latest systems that treat a wide range of tones with minimal discomfort.

Results You Can Feel, With Help Along the Way

We track your progress, schedule follow-ups, and guide you through long-term care.

Getting Ready for Your Laser Hair Removal Sessions

Before Your First Session

  • Don’t tan for four weeks
  • Don’t wax or pluck for four weeks (shaving is fine)
  • Shave the area 1–2 days before
  • Disclose medications, skin issues, and past treatments

On the Day of Treatment

  • Arrive with clean skin: no makeup, lotion, or deodorant
  • You may receive protective eyewear and numbing cream
  • The laser feels like quick snaps
  • Redness may occur but fades quickly

Aftercare

  • Avoid sun and use SPF 30+
  • Don’t pluck or wax between sessions
  • Shaving is okay
  • Follow all clinician instructions

Questions and Answers

Is laser hair removal permanent?

It significantly reduces hair but does not guarantee zero regrowth. Regrowth is usually lighter and finer.

Does it hurt?

Most describe it as a quick, mild snap.

How long do results last?

Results vary but can last years with proper maintenance.

How many sessions will I need?

Most clients need 3 to 8 sessions.

What body parts can be treated?

Nearly all: legs, underarms, bikini, face, back, chest, full body.

Conclusion

It’s time to switch to laser hair removal if you’re tired of constant shaving or waxing. NewDermaMed can help you find the best laser hair removal in downtown Toronto, compare prices, or locate “laser hair removal near me.”

We use cutting-edge technology, skilled doctors, and a personalized approach to provide safe, effective, and comfortable treatments.

Make your free consultation appointment today and start your journey toward smoother, more confident skin. NewDermaMed is your first step toward a hair-free future.

Rosacea affects more than just how you look it also affects how you feel how confident you are and how your skin acts every day. NewDermaMed believes that the best way to treat rosacea is with a full plan not just one solution. This guide will explain what rosacea is how to figure out what type you have what treatments are available including the best in clinic laser and light therapies and how to get your skin to stay calm and clear for a long time.

What Is Rosacea and Why Does It Happen

Rosacea is a long term skin condition that causes redness on the face visible blood vessels flushing and sometimes bumps that look like acne.
We don’t know exactly what causes it but some of the main ones are

  • Vascular reactivity blood vessels that easily flush or stay open
  • Long term swelling of the skin
  • Environmental and lifestyle factors including sun exposure consumption of hot or spicy foods alcohol intake and fluctuations in temperature
  • Skin barrier problems and skin that is too sensitive

There are many ways to treat skin problems and the best one depends on your symptoms skin type and what makes them worse.

Finding Out What Type of Rosacea You Have and Why It Matters

Common Subtypes

  • Erythematotelangiectatic rosacea causes redness on the face that won’t go away and small blood vessels that are easy to see
  • Papulopustular rosacea has red bumps and pustules that look a lot like acne
  • Rosacea phymatosa is skin that is thicker around the nose
  • Ocular rosacea causes eye irritation dryness and redness

Why the Best Treatment Depends on the Subtype

Each subtype reacts differently

  • Laser or light therapies work best on redness and visible blood vessels
  • Topical or oral medications work better for bumps and pustules
  • Thickening requires more aggressive or surgical methods

We make a personalized plan for you at NewDermaMed based on your skin type how often you have flare ups your skin tone and your lifestyle.

How to Get Rid of Rosacea A Multi Level Approach

To take care of rosacea well you need to control your lifestyle and triggers use topical and systemic treatments and get procedures or laser treatments.

Tier 1: Managing Lifestyle and Triggers

It is important to lower flare triggers before or during any procedure

  • Every day put on a broad spectrum sunscreen with a high SPF
  • Stay away from things that make you feel bad like very hot or very cold weather spicy foods alcohol and hard exercise without cooling down
  • Use skin care products that don’t have any scents or harsh exfoliants

This foundation makes skin more stable and helps treatments work better.

Tier 2: Topical and Oral Treatments

Depending on your subtype treatments may include

  • Azelaic acid ivermectin metronidazole or brimonidine as topical agents that can help with redness
  • Taking doxycycline in low doses by mouth to treat bumps or inflammation

These help keep inflammation in check lower breakouts and calm redness but they often need to be used consistently and may not completely get rid of visible vessels.

Tier 3: Advanced Treatments Laser and Intense Pulsed Light

In clinic treatments work very well for redness that won’t go away visible blood vessels or thickening skin

  • IPL or broadband light works on red spots and enlarged blood vessels
  • Pulsed dye laser PDL Nd YAG or KTP lasers can make your face less red and make your capillaries less visible
  • Resurfacing or fractional laser can make thickened or uneven skin texture better

We choose the safest and most effective technology for your skin type and rosacea subtype at NewDermaMed to get the best results with the least amount of downtime.

Making the Best Plan

The best way to treat rosacea is:

  • Depending on the type you have
  • Layered management of lifestyle medications and procedures
  • Made just for your skin tone way of life and goals
  • Long term focus on management and prevention instead of a quick fix

Why Laser Treatment Is Often the Best Way to Get Rid of Rosacea Redness That Wont Go Away

Laser and light based treatments are often the best way to get rid of redness visible vessels or flushing that happens a lot

  • They directly attack and shrink blood vessels that have become too big
  • They make the skin tone better overall and make the redness less visible
  • They can help people who need to use topical redness treatments every day do so less often

At NewDermaMed we use modern tools that work well on all skin tones to safely and effectively make things look better.

How to Choose the Right Clinic and What to Ask at NewDermaMed

Important Questions to Ask During Your Consultation

  • What are the most important signs of my illness redness bumps or thickening
  • What kind of laser or device will you use and is it safe for my skin tone
  • How many treatments do I need how much do they cost and how long will I be out of work
  • What kind of skin care and lifestyle plan should I follow between sessions

Why NewDermaMed Is the Best Partner for You

  • We offer in depth consultations to help you find your triggers and subtype
  • We have a full range of options such as medications lasers and advice on how to live a healthy life
  • We have worked with all skin tones and advanced laser systems before
  • Safety comfort and long term skin health are our top priorities

You don’t have to let rosacea control your skin or your self esteem. You can have skin that looks clearer calmer and healthier if you make a plan that works for your skin’s needs. posts.excerpt: Acne scars affect how you feel and how your skin reflects you, not just how you look. posts.content_html_rest:
Acne scars affect how you feel and how your skin reflects you, not just how you look. We know how annoying it can be to have a texture, indentation, or discoloration that won’t go away at NewDermaMed. We’re going deeper than just the surface in this guide. You’ll learn what acne scars are, why they form, how to pick the best treatment, and how you and your clinic can work together to get skin that looks smoother and healthier.

What Are Acne Scars and Why Do They Happen

What You Need to Know About Acne Scars

When acne breaks out, especially in deep or inflamed areas, the skin can change permanently in texture or colour as it heals. Changes in the skin’s surface, volume, or movement can cause acne scars.
In general, scars can look like this:

  • Indented or atrophic scars happen when there is a loss of volume or collagen.
  • Hypertrophic or keloid scars are raised scars that have too much collagen.
  • Changes in colour or post-inflammatory marks (changes in pigmentation rather than deep textural changes).

What Makes Acne Scar to Form?

Acne causes inflammation below the skin’s surface. If the body makes too little or too much collagen while it heals, it can leave a permanent mark. Too little collagen can cause depressions, and too much collagen can cause raised scars.
Other contributing factors include genetics, skin type, severity and duration of acne, whether it was picked or manipulated, and how the skin healed afterward.
Before we suggest any treatment at NewDermaMed, we make sure to find out what kind of scar it is.

How to Get Rid of Acne Scars: A Look at Acne Scar Treatments at NewDermaMed

Step 1: Get a Professional Opinion and a Plan Just for You

Before any treatment starts, your skin will be carefully examined. This includes your acne history, the state of your skin right now, the type of scars you have, your skin tone, and your way of life.
At NewDermaMed, we make treatment plans that are unique to each patient. These plans may include one or more therapies, depending on the type of scar, how much time you want to spend recovering, and your goals.

Step 2: Help at Home and on the Skin

In-clinic procedures are important, but excellent skincare is the most important thing. To make your skin look better, use products that contain retinoids, vitamin C, and AHAs or BHAs. Put on sunscreen every day to keep scars from getting darker or changing colours. Don’t pick at or squeeze acne lesions; this can make scars worse. To help your skin respond better to professional treatments, you need to do these things.

Step 3: Treatments for Acne Scars in the Clinic

Chemical Peels and Micro Abrasion

Chemical peels and microdermabrasion are examples of superficial to mid-depth treatments that can help smooth out rough skin and lighten dark spots. But for scars that are deeper, more advanced treatments are usually needed.

Microneedling or Radiofrequency Needling

Microneedling makes small controlled injuries to the skin to boost collagen production. This is beneficial for scars that are indented or atrophic. It makes skin tightening and deeper rejuvenation better when used with radiofrequency energy.

Fillers and Subcision

For deep rolling scars, subcision breaks up the fibrous scar tissue that is below the surface. Thereafter, you can use dermal fillers to lift scars that are depressed so they look smoother.

Treatments with Lasers and Light

Laser and fractional resurfacing are two of the best ways to make skin feel smoother, boost collagen, and fix rough spots. For safe and best results, different lasers may be used depending on your skin type.

Step 4: Keeping It Up and Having Realistic Expectations

It’s important to know that no treatment will get rid of scars right away, and getting rid of them completely is very rare. The goal is a big clear change for the better.
For best results, you may need to have several sessions spaced out over a few weeks. Taking good care of your skin at home, protecting it from the sun, and not getting new acne breakouts will help keep the progress you’ve made with your treatments.

Choosing the Right Clinic and Treatment What Makes NewDermaMed Different

Questions to Ask During Your Consultation

  • What kind of scars do I have from acne?
  • What is the best treatment for my skin tone and scar type?
  • Could you please let me know the number of sessions I will need and the expected waiting time?
  • What can I realistically expect to happen?
  • What do you need to do for aftercare?

Why You Should Choose NewDermaMed

We do the following at NewDermaMed:

  • Give full consultations to find out what kind of scars you have and what your skin needs.
  • For the best results, use advanced technology and various treatment options.
  • Give clear treatment timelines and prices that are easy to understand.
  • Help you make plans for aftercare and long-term maintenance to keep getting better.

Questions People Ask About Treating Acne Scars

Will Acne Scars Ever Go Away for Good?

It’s not common for full removal to happen, but with professional treatment and regular care, a big improvement is definitely possible.

What Is the Best Time to Get Rid of Acne Scars?

Once your acne is under control and your skin has healed enough to be treated safely. Acne treatment and scar correction often go hand in hand.

Will Treatments Work on Skin That Is Darker?

Yes definitely but the choice of treatment is important. Our team at NewDermaMed has a lot of experience working with all skin tones so you can be sure that the results will be safe and effective.

How Long Will I Be Out of Work?

It depends on the treatment:

  • Superficial peels and microneedling very little time off
  • Laser resurfacing a few days of redness or peeling
    We’ll go over everything in detail during your appointment.

Conclusion

Acne scars can make you think about the past but they don’t have to be part of your skin’s future if you use the right approach. If you have deep indentations uneven texture or dark marks on your skin professional treatments at NewDermaMed can help you get smoother clearer and more confident skin.

Are you ready to move on? Schedule an appointment with NewDermaMed today. Our team of experts will look at your skin talk to you about the best ways to treat your acne scars and help you get results that last. This is where your path to skin that is free of scars and full of confidence begins.

posts.title: What is PRP therapy and how does it help with skin rejuvenation or hair loss
posts.excerpt: There are always new treatments in dermatology and aesthetic medicine that use the body’s own healing power in amazing ways. A lot of people are talking about Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy, or PRP therapy for short. If you want to deal with hair loss, restore density, or make your skin feel and look better, PRP is […]
posts.content_html_rest:
There are always new treatments in dermatology and aesthetic medicine that use the body’s own healing power in amazing ways. A lot of people are talking about Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy, or PRP therapy for short. If you want to deal with hair loss, restore density, or make your skin feel and look better, PRP is an interesting option that is less invasive. We’ve seen at NewDermamed how this method can help people who want results that look natural based on biology. In this post, we’ll talk about what PRP therapy is, how it works for hair loss and skin rejuvenation, the treatment process, who it’s best for, what results to expect, and how to use it wisely.

What you should know about platelet rich plasma

PRP therapy works by taking a small sample of your blood and processing it to concentrate the platelets. Platelets are tiny cell fragments that are very important for healing and growth. When the platelets are concentrated and turned on, they release signalling proteins and growth factors that help tissues heal. Since the material is your own blood, the chances of an allergic reaction or rejection are very low.

What makes PRP so popular right now

Doctors first used PRP to fix tendons and ligaments in sports medicine, but they quickly learned that it could also help with hair restoration and cosmetic procedures. The appeal is that there isn’t much downtime, the ingredients are natural, and the body can heal itself instead of relying on synthetic products. We at NewDermamed believe that the link between natural healing and medical accuracy is what makes PRP so unique.

How PRP helps your hair-loss

How hair loss happens

Let’s go over the basics of hair growth and loss before we talk about how PRP works. There are three stages that hair follicles go through:
• Growth (anagen)
• Transition (catagen)
• Resting/shedding (telogen)

As we age or go through hormonal changes like androgenetic alopecia, the anagen phase gets shorter, the follicles get smaller (miniaturize), and the hair gets thinner and less pigmented.

How PRP helps hair grow back

When injected into the scalp, the concentrated platelets release growth factors such as PDGF, EGF, and VEGF. These make the scalp’s microenvironment better, boost blood flow, and wake up hair follicles that have been sleeping. PRP therapy for hair growth can:
• Improve blood flow and the delivery of nutrients to hair follicles
• Reduce swelling around hair roots
• Encourage the growth of new hair shafts and make them thicker
• Help grafts stay alive after a hair transplant

Profiles of candidates and what to expect

Hair PRP therapy is a good option for people who:
• Are men or women with early to moderate thinning hair instead of advanced baldness
• Are looking for natural, non-surgical solutions
• Want to improve the results of hair transplants
• Have realistic expectations of gradual improvement

Most plans say that treatments should happen once a month for three to four months, and then maintenance should happen every four to six months. After a few months, you should see a big difference as the follicles react to the stimulation.

How PRP helps your skin look younger

How skin repair works

PRP works to make skin look younger by injecting or microneedling concentrated growth factors deep into the dermis. These growth factors wake up fibroblasts, make more collagen and elastin, improve blood flow, and help skin cells grow back. Because of this, PRP helps fight the effects of aging, sun damage, and stress from the environment.

Uses

PRP therapy works well for:
• Fine lines and wrinkles
• Uneven texture and tone
• Acne scars and other mild scarring
• Skin that looks dull or tired
• Skin that has lost its firmness and elasticity

Normal procedure

A skin-focused PRP session usually has the following:

  1. A consultation and skin checkup
  2. A small blood test
  3. Centrifugation to separate the platelet-rich plasma
  4. Cleaning and numbing the skin
  5. Putting PRP on the skin with microneedling or direct injection
  6. Instructions for aftercare (protecting your skin from the sun and being gentle with it)

There isn’t much downtime, and redness or swelling only lasts a short time. The results show up slowly as the skin gets smoother and more radiant as collagen builds up.

What to expect from PRP therapy at NewDermamed

Individualized consultation and treatment plan

At Newdermamed, each PRP treatment is made just for you. During your consultation, we’ll go over:
• Your medical history and any underlying factors (like hormones or medications)
• The level of hair loss or skin problems
• What you want to happen and what you expect

After that, we’ll make a personalized treatment plan that may include PRP along with other advanced therapies like microneedling, laser treatments, or topical medications.

During your visit

Here’s what a typical PRP session looks like:
• A quick and simple blood draw
• Onsite preparation of PRP using specialized centrifugation
• Targeted delivery through scalp injections (for hair) or microneedling (for skin)
• Minimal downtime with immediate return to normal activity

Safety side effects and results

Because PRP comes from your own blood, allergic reactions are very rare. Possible minor effects include redness, swelling, or tenderness that subsides within 24 hours.

Keep in mind:
• Results vary by age, biology, and condition severity
• PRP is not an instant fix, but rather a regenerative boost
• Regular maintenance helps sustain long-term results
• Choosing a certified, experienced provider ensures the best outcome

At Newdermamed, we focus on safety, transparency, and long-term care for each client.

Comparing PRP for hair vs skin

Core similarities

Both PRP therapies:
• Use your own blood-derived platelets
• Stimulate natural regeneration
• Require consistency for optimal results
• Offer minimal downtime and a high safety profile

Key differences

• Target Area: Hair PRP focuses on the scalp and follicles, while skin PRP targets the dermis and surface layers
• Application Method: Hair PRP uses scalp injections, skin PRP uses microneedling or direct facial injections
• Treatment Frequency: Hair PRP typically requires monthly sessions then maintenance, skin PRP often involves two to three initial sessions followed by yearly touch-ups
• Goals: Hair PRP promotes hair density and strength, skin PRP improves tone, texture, and radiance
• Visible Results: Hair results may appear in 4–6 months, skin rejuvenation results can start showing within weeks and improve over time

Choosing the right treatment

If you’re experiencing hair thinning or early hair loss, PRP therapy for hair growth is ideal. If your concern is dullness, wrinkles, or uneven texture, PRP skin rejuvenation can restore your glow naturally. At NewDermamed, our experts can guide you through both options or combine them for comprehensive rejuvenation.

Realistic expectations and the holistic approach

Setting practical goals

PRP therapy works best as part of a broader wellness and beauty plan.

For hair, focus on:
• Balanced nutrition and scalp health
• Managing stress and hormones
• Regular maintenance treatments

For skin, support PRP with:
• Consistent sun protection
• Proper hydration and medical-grade skincare
• Healthy lifestyle choices and sleep

Results take time, but with consistency and care, the improvements are long-lasting and natural-looking.

Combining treatments for enhanced results

PRP can be combined with other treatments to amplify benefits:
• Hair PRP can complement laser therapy, growth serums, or hair transplants
• Skin PRP pairs beautifully with microneedling, laser resurfacing, and chemical peels

At NewDermamed, our specialists create holistic plans that maximize your investment and deliver truly rejuvenated results.

Conclusion

If you’re seeking a natural, medically advanced solution for thinning hair or aging skin, PRP therapy may be the perfect answer. By using your body’s own plasma to stimulate regeneration, it offers real, lasting results without surgery or harsh chemicals.

At NewDermamed, we combine scientific precision with compassionate care to help you achieve radiant skin and fuller, healthier hair. Ready to transform your confidence? Schedule your personalized consultation at NewDermamed today and discover how PRP therapy can help you look and feel your best naturally.

posts.excerpt: You are in the right place if you want to make your skin look better, feel better, and glow from the inside out. posts.content_html_rest:
You are in the right place if you want to make your skin look better, feel better, and glow from the inside out. At NewDermaMed, we love helping you learn everything you need to know about advanced skincare treatments so you can make an informed choice. We’ll go into great detail about microdermabrasion in this post. We’ll talk about what it is, how it works, the benefits, how it compares to other treatments like microneedling, and what you should know if you’re thinking about getting it.

What Is Microdermabrasion?

Microdermabrasion is a cosmetic procedure that doesn’t hurt and gently removes the top layer of skin. The treatment uses mechanical abrasion, usually with fine crystals or a diamond-tipped wand and suction, to buff away dead skin cells, encourage new skin growth, and show off the smoother, fresher skin underneath.

Microdermabrasion started out as a gentler alternative to deeper resurfacing treatments, but now it’s the go-to method for making skin look younger with little downtime.

What Is the Process of Microdermabrasion?

How It Works

The treatment usually has two main parts:

  • A handheld device uses crystals, diamond tips, or bristle-based heads to abrade the stratum corneum, which is the outermost layer of skin.
  • At the same time, suction removes dead skin cells and debris, leaving the area clean and ready for new growth.

The process causes mild damage to the skin’s surface, which increases blood flow and collagen production. This makes the skin look healthier and firmer.

What to Expect During Treatment

This is how a typical microdermabrasion session goes:

  • Consultation and skin assessment
  • Cleaning
  • Exfoliation using a crystal or diamond-tip wand
  • Application of soothing serums, moisturizers, and SPF
  • Aftercare advice

Number of Sessions and Upkeep

Microdermabrasion only works on the top layer of skin, so the effects build up over time. Many clinics suggest a series of treatments, usually 4 to 10 sessions spaced 2 to 4 weeks apart. After the first course, regular maintenance sessions help keep the skin looking fresh.

Microdermabrasion Facial Benefits: Better Tone and Texture

Microdermabrasion helps smooth out rough spots, even out skin texture, and improve overall skin tone by getting rid of the dead skin cells on the surface and encouraging collagen renewal.

Less Visible Pores, Sun Damage, and Fine Lines

Microdermabrasion works well for a number of common problems, such as enlarged pores, light sun spots, mild acne scars, and fine lines. The procedure gently resurfaces the skin, which often makes pores less visible and skin look brighter.

Better Absorption of Skin Care Products

Your skin can better absorb serums and moisturizers now that the dead skin cells are gone. This makes your daily skincare routine work better.

Little Downtime and a Wide Range of Uses

Microdermabrasion is quick (usually 20 to 40 minutes), comfortable, and doesn’t require much downtime. It is usually good for a wide range of skin types.

More Blood Flow and Shine

The suction and rubbing increase blood flow, which can make your skin look more radiant and healthy, giving you that “fresh” look.

Which One Should You Choose: Microdermabrasion or Microneedling?

How Deep the Treatment Goes

Microdermabrasion works on the top layer of skin to fix texture, tone, and minor surface problems.
Microneedling uses tiny needles to go deeper into the dermis and stimulate collagen for deeper wrinkles, scars, and other concerns.

Feeling and Recovery

Microdermabrasion: Little to no downtime, a little redness, and not much pain.
Microneedling: More downtime (redness, possible peeling), more moderate pain, and longer recovery.

What Concerns Are Ideal

Choose microdermabrasion if you want to improve skin texture, brightness, pore size, minor sun damage, and product absorption.

Choose microneedling for scars, deeper wrinkles, stretch marks, or stronger collagen effects.

Using Together

At NewDermaMed, we often suggest using these treatments together. Start with microdermabrasion to refresh the surface, then move to microneedling for deeper work if needed.

Who Is a Good Fit and Who Should Be Careful?

The Best Candidates

  • People whose skin is rough or uneven
  • Large pores, small sun damage, or surface blemishes
  • Those who want a quick pick-me-up with little downtime
  • Clients who want to enhance their skincare routine

When to Be Careful

  • Active acne breakouts, open wounds, or serious skin conditions
  • Recent isotretinoin use or deep chemical peels
  • Recent sunburn or tanning

A proper skin assessment and consultation are important for safety.

Before Treatment: Get the Most Out of Your Results

  • Avoid sun exposure and tanning for at least a week
  • Stop using harsh exfoliants or strong active products a few days before
  • Arrive with no makeup, heavy creams, or oils on your face

The Day of Treatment

After the treatment, you can expect cleansing, a treatment wand, and calming products. Most people say the feeling is pleasant, like a light scrub with suction. Some versions now include serum infusion for deeper ingredient penetration.

Aftercare

  • Avoid scrubs or harsh treatments for a few days
  • Use gentle cleanser and moisturizer
  • Wear broad-spectrum SPF daily
  • Avoid saunas, hot tubs, and direct sunlight for 24–48 hours
  • Resume normal skincare but avoid strong actives until healed

Taking Care Of Your Skin Afterward

Depending on goals, many clients schedule follow-up appointments every 4 to 8 weeks. For long-lasting results, combine microdermabrasion with good skincare and sun protection.

Why NewDermaMed Is Your Partner in Choosing the Right Clinic

Personalized Skin Analysis and Customized Plans

Your skin history, concerns, lifestyle, and goals shape every treatment plan.

New Tools and Techniques

We stay current with advancements like diamond-tip microdermabrasion with serum infusions.

Safe Protocols and Caring Professionals

Every procedure follows strict care standards. Your comfort, safety, and results are top priorities.

We Value Open Communication

We provide clear expectations, treatment plans, cost breakdowns, and aftercare instructions.

Questions and Answers About Microdermabrasion

Does microdermabrasion hurt?

Most people find the treatment comfortable with light scratching or suction.

How long will it take to see results?

You may see a glow right away, but full changes usually require a series of treatments.

Is there any downtime?

Minimal, slight redness or sensitivity for a day or two.

How often can I do it?

Every 2 to 4 weeks for a series, then periodic maintenance.

Can it be used on the body?

Yes, neck, chest, hands, back, and other areas.

Conclusion

Microdermabrasion is a strong and easy treatment that can make your skin look better, feel better, and fit into your routine. It’s great for many skin types, requires little downtime, and pairs well with other treatments.

At NewDermaMed, we’re dedicated to helping you every step of the way, from choosing the right treatment to aftercare and maintenance.

Want to improve your skin? Schedule your personalized consultation with NewDermaMed now. We’ll assess your skin and create a plan so you feel confident, refreshed, and glowing.

posts.title: What Is Laser Hair Removal And How Does It Work?
posts.excerpt: If you’ve ever wondered if you could skip shaving, waxing, or all those painful plucks and have smoother skin instead, you’re in the right place. People ask us a lot at NewDermaMed, “What is laser hair removal?” Let’s talk about what laser hair removal is, how it works, why so many people choose it, what […]
posts.content_html_rest:
If you’ve ever wondered if you could skip shaving, waxing, or all those painful plucks and have smoother skin instead, you’re in the right place. People ask us a lot at NewDermaMed, “What is laser hair removal?” Let’s talk about what laser hair removal is, how it works, why so many people choose it, what “IPL laser hair removal” means, how long the results can last, and what you should know before you book your sessions.

What You Need To Know About Laser Hair Removal

What Is Laser Hair Removal Exactly

Laser hair removal is a cosmetic procedure that uses focused beams of light energy to get rid of unwanted hair at the root. The goal is to hurt the hair follicle so that it stops or slows down making new hair. Laser hair removal is different from shaving or waxing because it doesn’t just get rid of hair; it also tries to slow down hair growth over time.

We don’t just see laser hair removal as a cosmetic convenience at NewDermaMed. We see it as a long-term investment in your skin and grooming routine.

How Does It Work?

Here’s the science behind it: each hair goes through a cycle that includes phases of growth (anagen), transition (catagen), and resting/shedding (telogen). A laser can only effectively target follicles in the active growth phase because the pigment (melanin) in the hair absorbs the light energy.

This method is called selective photothermolysis. Melanin in the hair shaft absorbs the laser light and turns it into heat, which then kills or hurts the follicle and its ability to grow hair again.

A lot of sessions are needed because only a small number of hairs are growing at once. Most people go back to their normal activities after a short time. We make it clear at NewDermaMed how many sessions you will probably need based on your skin tone, hair type, and area of treatment.

What About IPL And Laser

A lot of the time, you’ll hear “IPL laser hair removal”. IPL stands for “intense pulsed light”. It’s not a real laser; it’s a broad spectrum light source that can remove hair by heating the follicle in a similar way. IPL might work for some people, but high-spec lasers are more accurate and usually safer for more skin tones. We use fully regulated medical lasers at NewDermaMed to make sure that the technology is right for your skin type, hair colour, and the area being treated.

Why More People Choose Laser Hair Removal

People choose laser over shaving, waxing, or plucking for a lot of different reasons:

  • Results that last longer: Laser hair removal slows hair growth down more than most temporary methods.
  • Less upkeep: After your first set of treatments and a few touch-ups, you don’t have to shave as often or at all.
  • Better skin texture: You won’t have as many ingrown hairs, irritation, or bumps on your skin because you don’t wax, pluck, or shave as often.
  • Speed: With modern equipment, it doesn’t take long to treat large areas like the legs and back.
  • Laser hair removal can be used on almost any part of the body, from the face to the underarms, bikini line, and full legs.

The Perfect Candidate

Laser hair removal works for a lot of people, but it works best when:

  • The laser works best on people with dark, coarse hair and lighter skin.
  • Good overall health and no active skin infections or major skin problems in the area being treated.
  • Be willing to go to more than one session and take good care of yourself before and after (like staying out of the sun).

At NewDermaMed, we look at each person’s hair colour, skin tone, medical history, and what they want to see happen to see if laser hair removal is a good option for them.

What To Expect: The Treatment Journey At NewDermaMed

First Meeting

A personal consultation is where your journey begins. We will look at:

  • The parts of your body that you want treated, like your legs, underarms, bikini area, face, back, etc.
  • The colour, texture, and thickness of your hair
  • Your skin tone and any past hair removal you may have done
  • Your promise to go to follow-up sessions and take care of yourself afterward
  • Any medical history or drugs that could affect treatment

Getting Ready For Treatment

You need to do a few important things ahead of time to get the best results:

  • For a few weeks before treatment, don’t go outside in the sun or tan.
  • The day before your session, shave the area.
  • Don’t wax, pluck, or use hair removal creams for a few weeks before the session.

At NewDermaMed, we give you detailed instructions before your treatment so that you are ready and everything goes smoothly.

The Treatment Session

You will wear protective glasses during the session. You can protect your skin by using a cooling gel or device. The laser handpiece is put on the skin, and the energy pulses go straight to the follicles. A lot of clients say it feels like a snap or a warm sting.

Depending on how big the area is, a session can last anywhere from a few minutes (for the upper lip) to an hour (for the full legs). You might feel a little red or like you have a sunburn after the session. Most people go back to their normal activities right away.

Aftercare And Post Treatment

After treatment, you should:

  • For several weeks, stay out of the sun and tanning beds.
  • Don’t take hot baths, go to saunas, or work out hard for at least 24 to 48 hours.
  • You can shave the hair in the treated area, but don’t wax, pluck, or bleach it.
  • Expect some hair to fall out over the next 1 to 3 weeks.

We check in with you at NewDermaMed to see how your skin is doing and set up the next appointment.

How Long Does Laser Hair Removal Last

One of the most common questions is how long does laser hair removal last? The truth is that laser hair removal isn’t always “permanent” in the strictest sense, but it does often slow down hair growth and make fewer hairs visible for many months or even years.

This is what you can really expect:

How Does It Work?

Here’s the science behind it: each hair goes through a cycle that includes phases of growth (anagen), transition (catagen), and resting/shedding (telogen). A laser can only effectively target follicles in the active growth phase because the pigment (melanin) in the hair absorbs the light energy.

This method is called selective photothermolysis. Melanin in the hair shaft absorbs the laser light and turns it into heat, which then kills or hurts the follicle and its ability to grow hair again.

posts.content_html_rest:
Surgery is no longer the only way to make your face look younger. Juvederm and other treatments can help you look younger by enhancing your features, smoothing out fine lines, and adding volume to your face. All of this can be done in a short amount of time and with results that look natural.

At NewDermaMed Toronto, we use Juvederm injectable fillers to make you look fresh, balanced, and confident without changing who you are. This guide will help you understand what to expect from one of the most trusted brands of dermal fillers in the world, whether you’re looking into what Juvederm is or how long it lasts.

What Is Juvederm?

Juvederm is a dermal filler made with hyaluronic acid (HA) that adds volume, smooths out lines, and improves the shape of the face. Hyaluronic acid is a natural substance in your skin that keeps it hydrated, full, and flexible. As we get older, our HA levels drop, which can make our skin look less firm or defined over time.

That’s when Juvederm comes in. This injectable filler adds volume and moisture back to areas that have lost them while also bringing out your natural beauty. It doesn’t require surgery or a long recovery time.

Our medical injectors at NewDermaMed use Juvederm to give you smooth, natural-looking results that are perfect for your face shape and aesthetic goals. Every shot is done with care and skill to make sure that your look stays natural and expressive.

What Is Juvederm Made Of?

Hyaluronic acid is the main ingredient in Juvederm, which is what you need to know. This sugar molecule that is found in nature pulls in and holds onto water in the skin, giving it volume and moisture.

Different types of Juvederm are made for different things. Some are made to fill in lines, while others are made to add shape or fullness. They all have one thing in common: they all work well with your skin’s own tissue.

Juvederm also has lidocaine in it, which is a mild numbing agent that makes the treatment more comfortable. At NewDermaMed, we tailor each Juvederm treatment to meet your specific needs by using the right type and amount of filler. This level of accuracy makes sure that your results look balanced and not too full or fake.

Why Pick Juvederm?

There are many dermal fillers on the market today, but Juvederm is still one of the most trusted and cutting-edge. Health Canada has approved it, and skilled doctors worldwide have been using it for years.

People in Toronto love Juvederm because:

  • Results that happen right away and get better over time
  • The filler moves with your facial expressions, so it looks and feels natural
  • Hydration and rejuvenation that lasts a long time
  • A simple in-clinic treatment with little downtime
  • Safe and biocompatible formula that works for most skin types

Juvederm is a flexible and effective way to improve your lips, define your jawline, smooth out smile lines, or just make you look better overall.

Juvederm Is Often Used to Treat These Areas

Juvederm is versatile; it can improve the look of different areas of the face. Some common areas for treatment are:

  • Lips for a little extra volume and shape
  • Cheeks to add volume and lift, like when you were young
  • Jawline for better shape and definition
  • Smile lines (nasolabial folds) for a smoother look
  • Lines around the mouth that look like marionettes provide balance
  • Chin enhancement for a more defined profile
  • Hollows under the eyes to appear more awake and refreshed

At NewDermaMed Toronto, we always tailor our services to each client. Before making your Juvederm treatment plan, we look at the proportions of your face, how it moves, and what you want to look like.

The Juvederm Injectable Filler Process

The Juvederm injectable filler procedure is quick, accurate, and doesn’t require much cutting. It usually takes 30 to 45 minutes.

What to expect:

  • Consultation: We start with a one-on-one consultation to learn about your goals, the structure of your face, and your medical history. We’ll work together to pick the Juvederm product that works best for you.
  • Getting ready: The area to be treated is cleaned, and a topical numbing agent may be used to make it more comfortable. Most clients say that the Juvederm procedure is effortless to handle because it already has lidocaine in it.
  • Injection: Your injector carefully puts the filler into specific areas using small, precise needles or cannulas, shaping it and blending it perfectly with your natural contours.
  • Refinement: After the injections are done, your injector will carefully smooth and shape the area so that it looks even and natural.

You will see an immediate difference, and the full results will show up over the coming days as the filler settles.

How Long Does Juvederm Last?

People often ask us how long Juvederm lasts.

How long your results last depends on the product you use, the area being treated, and how fast your body burns calories. The effects of Juvederm usually last for 9 to 18 months. Some formulations, like those used for deeper contouring, like the jawline or cheeks, can last even longer.

As time goes on, your body naturally breaks down the hyaluronic acid in Juvederm and absorbs it safely. To keep their results steady and fresh, many clients choose to get maintenance treatments once or twice a year.

Your injector at NewDermaMed will help you figure out the best schedule to keep your desired look while keeping your results natural and subtle.

What Makes Juvederm Better Than Other Fillers?

There are many different kinds of dermal fillers, but Juvederm is the best because it has a smooth texture and lasts a long time.

Juvederm products use advanced Vycross™ technology to link hyaluronic acid molecules together better. This makes the filler blend in better with your skin and last longer than other types.

This makes Juvederm a great choice for anyone who wants a safe treatment, works as expected, and looks great.

Is Juvederm Safe?

Yes, for sure. Health Canada and the FDA both approve Juvederm. It is one of the most researched and trusted dermal fillers in the world. When done by trained professionals, like the medical staff at NewDermaMed Toronto, it is both safe and very effective.

Hyaluronic acid, a natural skin component, makes allergic reactions rare. Before we start treatment, our team will talk to you about everything to make sure you’re comfortable, safe, and a good fit for Juvederm.

What to Expect After Treatment

You can go back to most of your normal activities right away after getting Juvederm injectable filler. You might notice some mild swelling or pain, but this usually goes away in a day or two.

We suggest the following to help your skin settle nicely:

  • Not doing any intense exercise for 24 hours
  • Keeping treated areas clean and free of makeup for the first day
  • Avoiding very hot or very cold weather
  • Lying on your back to keep pressure off the area

Your injector will give you full post-op care instructions to ensure a smooth recovery.

The Results: Confident, Natural, and Subtle

At NewDermaMed, we believe that every improvement should look natural, balanced, and like you.

That’s precisely what Juvederm helps us do. The results are clear but not too much, giving you a fresh look that feels real and makes your beauty even better.

A lot of our clients say that the experience gives them more confidence, which is the kind of change that makes them look as lively and energetic as they feel.

Using Juvederm With Other Treatments

Juvederm can be used with other non-surgical treatments at NewDermaMed to make a more complete plan for rejuvenation. These include:

  • Botox to smooth out expression lines
  • Thread lifts for lifting and defining
  • Laser treatments to make skin feel better
  • Long-term skin health treatments that boost collagen

Our team will make a plan just for you to help you get the results you want in a safe and natural way.

Reasons to Choose NewDermaMed Toronto for Juvederm
